clue.text: Drink tax ending and bringing back atmosphere of city

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer, a drink

indicators.note: ending points to the final letter of the word tax beside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: bringing back tells you to write the word for atmosphere backwards

parts.note: atmosphere means air

explanation.surface: Abolishing a duty on alcohol restores the old mood of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the X of tax, and 'bringing back' turns AIR into RIA. The word 'and' is not a joiner here but three letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the great Egyptian port on the Mediterranean founded by Alexander the Great.

clue.text: Room, possibly, for a wager

definitions.meaning: this prefix meaning before can be followed by room, giving a small chamber that leads into a larger one
the stake each poker player puts in before the deal

explanation.surface: There may be space to place a bet.
explanation.definitionFit: A prefix that goes in front of room to name a waiting chamber, and also the poker stake put up before cards are dealt.

clue.text: Measures lines between points

indicators.note: between places the letters for lines in the middle of the two compass letters

parts.note: E, east, is a point of the compass
S, south, is another point of the compass
L is the abbreviation for line, so two lines are LL

explanation.surface: Someone works out the length of lines drawn from one dot to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts LL inside two compass points, E and S. The word 'Measures' reads as a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Old units of length, about 45 inches in England, used for cloth.

clue.text: Legislative Council put limit on car producer

parts.note: a legislative council is an assembly, a body that makes laws
a line is a limit, as in drawing the line

explanation.surface: A law-making body imposes a cap on a motor manufacturer.
explanation.walkthrough: The car producer is not a firm but the factory method by which cars are built.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword-style description: the moving factory sequence on which motor vehicles are put together.

clue.text: Funny old penny loaf

parts.note: D was the abbreviation for the penny in British money before 1971, from the Latin denarius
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: An amusing loaf that costs a penny in old money.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: amusing in a dry or odd way.

clue.text: Be anxious to give support to language course

indicators.note: in a down clue the word that supports stands underneath, so the worrying comes below the language

parts.note: Irish is the Gaelic language of Ireland
to stew is to fret or worry

explanation.surface: A student is keen to back a series of language lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to give support to' places STEW beneath IRISH in this down entry. The course is one served at a meal, not a series of lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a dish of mutton, potatoes and onions served as part of a meal.

clue.text: Old king of note

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa musical scale

explanation.surface: A former monarch who was well known.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' reads as meaning famous, but it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the eighth-century ruler of Mercia who built a dyke along the Welsh border.

clue.text: It's very antiquated to have different sizes of lid

indicators.note: different says the letters of the three words after it are put in another order

explanation.surface: It is terribly old-fashioned to stock lids in several sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges SIZES OF LID into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative synonym: turned to stone with age, so hopelessly out of date.

clue.text: Opponent in a new game, bowling first

parts.note: tag is the children's chasing game
in cricket a bowler who is on is the one currently bowling
first written in figures is 1st, and the 1 is read as the letter I

explanation.surface: The other side in a fresh match starts by bowling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a player who is 'on' is bowling, and 'first' is 1ST with the figure read as an I.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an adversary, one who contends against another.

clue.text: Select funny old film, capable of enlargement

indicators.note: funny in the sense of odd says the letters of the word before it are disturbed

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a film

explanation.surface: Choose an amusing vintage movie that could be blown up for a bigger screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: made of sliding sections that extend, or able to magnify as an optical instrument does.

clue.text: Extra message — a way to attract attention

parts.note: PS, a postscript, is an extra message added after a letter is signed
St, short for street, is a way

explanation.surface: A further note is one method of getting noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose description: the hissed sound someone makes on purpose to catch another's ear quietly.

clue.text: Drawing, for example

definitions.meaning: a picture drawn to accompany a text
an instance given to make a point clear

explanation.definitionFit: Both a picture in a book and an instance that clarifies a point go by this name.

clue.text: Writing about entirely gripping plot

indicators.note: about says the abbreviation for writing is turned round

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing
all means entirely, as in all alone
holding means gripping in the hand

explanation.surface: An article concerning a thoroughly exciting storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MS into SM. The plot is a piece of land, not a story.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: in Britain a little farm or piece of land rented for cultivation.

clue.text: The whole body of legislators beginning to cheer

parts.note: Members of Parliament, the legislators, are called members
a cheer starts hip, hip before the hooray

explanation.surface: Every one of the lawmakers starts to applaud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to cheer' is not a first letter but the opening word of 'hip, hip, hooray'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the collective sense: all those who belong to a society taken together.

clue.text: Deceive partner about amount accomplished

indicators.note: about puts the words for deceive and partner round the word for amount

parts.note: to con is to trick or deceive
a mate is a partner
a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: Someone lied to their spouse over how much they had achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a container signal, not 'concerning'. 'accomplished' wants to be a past tense; it is an adjective meaning highly skilled.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as an adjective: supremely skilled, as of an artist or a liar.

clue.text: O'Neill met trouble with something soothing

indicators.note: trouble as a verb says the letters of the two words before it are disturbed

explanation.surface: A man called O'Neill ran into difficulty carrying a calming remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges ONEILL MET into the answer; 'met trouble' is not one phrase here.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a cream or lotion that softens and calms the skin.

clue.text: Arrangement for piano. — the one from Africa

indicators.note: an arrangement is a reordering, here of the words that follow

parts.note: the number one written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A piece of keyboard music, the one that came from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement for' looks like a musical term but signals the anagram, and 'one' is the Roman numeral standing among the letters being reordered.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: belonging to a country in the Horn of that continent, once called Abyssinia.

clue.text: Marriage to Jack, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a wedded joining of two people
the British national flag is named by this word followed by Jack

explanation.definitionFit: A wedded partnership, and the first word of the name of Britain's flag.

clue.text: Sister Isabella's overhead cover

parts.note: in Keats's poem Isabella, the heroine's brothers murder her lover and she buries his head in a pot under a herb plant, which thus grows over the head

explanation.surface: A nun's hat or veil.
explanation.walkthrough: Isabella is the sister of the murderous brothers in Keats's poem, not a nun; the 'overhead cover' is the herb she grows over her lover's buried head.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary allusion: the herb planted in the pot in Keats's poem, growing above the buried head.

clue.text: Pieces with zero seconds to move

indicators.note: to move says the letters of the two words before are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Chessmen and no time left on the clock to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges WITH ZERO into HOWITZER. The pieces are artillery pieces, not chessmen.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: short guns that lob shells at a high angle, called artillery pieces.

clue.text: Gladiator's death made this Caesar, for instance, leave

parts.note: Caesar is an example of a Roman
leave is time off work, a holiday

explanation.surface: A fighter dying in the arena caused the emperor to walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition quotes Byron's dying gladiator, 'butchered to make a Roman holiday'. 'leave' is a noun here, time off.
explanation.definitionFit: A quotation: Byron's Childe Harold has the arena fighter butchered to provide this entertainment.

clue.text: Form an idea

definitions.meaning: a likeness or shape, as in made in God's likeness
a picture held in the mind

explanation.definitionFit: A likeness or outward shape, and also a mental picture or conception.

clue.text: Failing to hold the job

definitions.meaning: a moral fault or bad habit
the bench tool whose jaws clamp the piece being worked on, which a craftsman calls the job

explanation.surface: Someone is unable to stay in employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral weakness, and the clamp on a workbench that grips the work.

clue.text: Some key, otherwise known as an island

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A certain cay that also goes by the name of island.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a small piece of land in a river, especially the Thames.

clue.text: Blue, perhaps, after hard frost

indicators.note: after says the rower follows the letter for hard

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils
a Blue is someone who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University at sport, and a rowing Blue is an oar, meaning an oarsman

explanation.surface: Feeling cold and miserable following a severe freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts OAR behind H. A Blue is an Oxford or Cambridge sportsman, and one who rows is called an oar.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the white coating of frozen dew seen on a cold morning.

clue.text: The handicap of many is cleverness

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number, which crosswords call many
cleverness is ability, mental skill

explanation.surface: Lots of people are held back by being too bright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'many' is the Roman numeral D, 500, by an old crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something that puts a person at a disadvantage.

clue.text: Huntsman put through the hoop?

definitions.meaning: John, the Cumberland fox hunter of the song D'ye ken John ...
in croquet, to send another player's ball through a hoop

explanation.surface: A rider to hounds is given a gruelling test.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the fox hunter in an English folk song, and a croquet term for knocking another ball through its hoop.

clue.text: Burial service covering knight in captivity

indicators.note: covering says the word for a burial goes round the chess letter

parts.note: an interment is the burying of a body
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A funeral rite for a knight who died as a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' wraps INTERMENT round N, the chess notation for knight.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: confinement of people, especially aliens or prisoners in wartime.
